div.p: * I have only seen a very small subset of customers that had limitations on the data leaving EMEA or the hosted region as an example, usually related to compliance like PCI. In those cases we either leveraged location specific scanners/gateways with external database or a completely separate Aqua control plane if the data could not be stored external. The data that is propagated from enforcers > gateway > database is mainly host metadata, vulnerability and CIS benchmarks scans as well as container runtime metadata and events. The KubeEnforcer also propagates Kubernetes cluster details and resources. You can review the type of data that is propagated in your environment under Workloads, Security Reports > CIS Benchmarks and Audit (e.g. toggle Audit Type to Container Runtime). I will also note that the Aqua components use a secure GRPC connection over HTTPS to communicate and also supports mTLS.

* The Advanced Deployment Architecture (recommended architecture) supports roughly 10K Enforcers and 500K workloads. We also include component resource recommendations in the Sizing Guide depending on environment size

* When the Enforcer goes into a disconnected state but is still running, it will continue to do so with the information previously supplied. This means that all existing policies and images will be enforced/audited, and the Enforcer will not be updated automatically with any policy or image updates. Once connectivity is restored, the Enforcer will update and process new information as expected.
